calls.title: James Berry and Chris Sanders
calls.summary: The team discussed how GrowthBook handles user bucketing and traffic allocation to run controlled experiments effectively. Key points included stable variant assignment via hashing user IDs, controlled traffic rollout using a slider bar, and namespace partitioning to prevent experiment overlap. The importance of proper experiment editing and safeguards against data corruption was emphasized. Experiment creation involves defining user attributes, targeting, linking to feature flags, and using a visual editor for no-code variant adjustments. Metrics are analyzed through data warehouses, employing both Bayesian and Frequentist algorithms to determine experiment outcomes. Ongoing support, expert user identification, and maintaining data governance were also highlighted.
calls.keywords: Growth Book, experimentation, feature flags, namespaces, traffic allocation, experiment results
